title: Finite pure-tensor coordinates of the ordered negative Koszul tensors
statement: Let (C,J,O) be a small ringed site with commutative ring sheaf O [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], A a commutative ring and rho:A -> Gamma(O) a coefficient map. Let a:Fin r -> A, allowing r=0. For the actual ordered negative Koszul tensor functors T_m(K)=K tensor_O tensor_i[O --rho(a_i)^(m+1)--> O] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], there are degreewise finite-subset coordinate isomorphisms T_m(K)^q = direct_sum_I K^(q+|I|), natural transition maps T_(m+1)->T_m and natural inclusions K->T_m satisfying the differential, coefficient-map, transition, and inclusion matrix equations of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model]. The coordinate inclusions are precisely the pure tensors ringedNegativeKoszulSummand, and the inclusions commute with the transitions. Each functor T_m preserves quasi-isomorphisms of arbitrary unbounded complexes. This finite statement involves no products, fibre, localization or coefficient-functor comparison.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, finite free negative Koszul complexes; finite-coordinate expansion in steps 1 and 3 of lem-cbc-exact-linear-koszul-fiber

proof.text: Use the normalized finite subset decomposition and its differential matrix. Derive the diagonal matrix for coefficient maps, rather than assume it: naturality of the total tensor inclusions, the tensor bifunctor and the inverse right unitor gives naturality of ringedNegativeKoszulSummand. Substitute the normalization, cancel the coordinate isomorphisms and apply the biproduct Kronecker identities.

For each subset I put p(I)=product over i in I of a_i. Define the degreewise transition by conjugating the biproduct diagonal with entries rho(p(I)) times identity by the coordinate isomorphisms at m+1 and m. Its row and column identities reduce the chain condition to scalar multiplication of differential entries. On the diagonal it is immediate. For an erased index use prod(I)=a_i prod(I.erase i), the power identity, and commutativity to prove p(I) coefficient_m(I,L)=coefficient_(m+1)(I,L) p(L); distribute the scalar over the finite sum. The diagonal coefficient-map matrices give naturality. This constructs a chain natural transformation, with exactly the required transition matrix.

Construct the inclusion in degree q by the equality transport K^q to K^(q+0), the empty-subset biproduct injection, and the inverse coordinates. The empty row of the differential matrix gives its chain equation: its erased-index sum is empty. The degree equality q=(q+1)+|I| is impossible. The already derived coefficient-map matrix gives naturality, using naturality of the equality transports. The biproduct Kronecker identities give the stated inclusion matrix, since q=q+|I| holds exactly for the empty subset. Apply the transition row identity at the empty subset; its scalar is the empty product one, so the inclusions commute with transitions.

Prove quasi-isomorphism preservation independently of the coordinate calculation. A negative double factor is zero off degrees -1 and 0, and in both supported degrees is isomorphic to the tensor unit, hence flat. Apply the existing proved source bounded-flat K-flat criterion CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat (the bounded sublemma in the module of lem-sfb-bounded-above-flat-kflat). The empty ordered tensor is K-flat because it is the tensor unit, and closure of the quasi-isomorphism K-flat object property under tensor products proves K-flatness of the ordered tensor by induction on r. Its right-whiskering property then gives the required quasi-isomorphism for every unbounded coefficient complex.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul. K2 proves the scalar-diagonal transitions, empty inclusions and their compatibility in Lean, derives coefficient-map naturality from actual tensors, and uses the proved generic bounded-flat K-flat criterion for quasi-isomorphism preservation; only the normalized tensor decomposition and its differential matrix remain a separate obligation.
